transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... my mom brought me. She keeps asking what's wrong, but I... I barely have the energy to answer her anymore. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything. I just sit in my room. I think I've had these same clothes on for a few days. 

I used to do things, you know? Like I used to knit, and journal, and go walking. I liked walking by the park because there was this one tree that looked like a giant hand. And I was knitting this scarf with purple yarn. I don't even like purple, really. It reminds me of grape soda, and one time when I was little I spilled grape soda all over my light-up shoes. They were my absolute favorite shoes. They stopped lighting up after that, the sticky stuff just ruined the little lights in the heels. 

But yeah, I don't knit now. I don't journal or go out walking like I used to. I don't do any of that. I just sit there.
When did you first notice that you started losing interest in things you used to enjoy like knitting and walking?

I think... it started right around when I began that community-college program. That was, um, about two years and two months ago. I remember because I had to go in early that first week to get my student ID printed. 

The lady at the desk taking the pictures was chewing this really strong peppermint gum. You could smell it from all the way across the room. She had this bright pink lipstick on, and it kept getting on her front teeth every time she talked. I wanted to tell her, but I just watched it. She was wearing this huge silver necklace, too, with a giant turquoise stone right in the middle of it. It looked so heavy, like it would just drag your neck down and make it ache if you wore it all day. I always wonder why people wear heavy jewelry like that. My aunt used to wear these massive hoop earrings, and her earlobes got all stretched out and droopy. It looked like melted wax. I don't like earrings. I never got my ears pierced because I don't want holes in my body that aren't supposed to be there.
Over these past two years, have there been times when you felt better and had more energy and interest in things, or has it pretty much been the same low mood and lack of motivation the whole time?

I'm not really sure... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling any better. It just feels like it's been exactly the same this whole time. It all just kind of... blends together, you know? 

Like when you mix way too many paint colors together on a palette and it just turns into that ugly, muddy brown color. We had to mix paints a lot in my high school art class. My teacher, Mr. Davis, he had these tiny round glasses that sat right on the very edge of his nose. I used to just stare at them the whole period, waiting for them to fall off into the dirty paint water. The paint cups always smelled so bad, kind of like old pennies. I really hate the smell of pennies. If you hold change in your hand for too long, your skin just smells like metal for the rest of the day. My mom keeps this huge glass jar of pennies in the kitchen right next to the microwave. The microwave is broken, actually, the little glass plate inside doesn't spin around anymore. So if you put anything in there, the middle stays completely frozen but the edges get so hot they burn the roof of your mouth. I burned my mouth on a pizza roll once and the skin peeled off for a week.
Before this started two years ago when you began college, had you ever experienced a period of time where you felt depressed, had low energy, or lost interest in things for weeks or months at a time?

Um, no, I don't think so. I don't remember ever feeling like that before. I was mostly just normal in high school. I actually really liked the end of high school because of the graduation ceremony. We had to wear these shiny blue gowns, and they were made out of this really weird, cheap material. It made this loud swooshing sound every time you moved your arms, kind of like a windbreaker jacket. 

My dad has this really old, neon green windbreaker that he wears every single time he mows the lawn. The grass clippings always stick to the bottom of it. I can't stand the smell of cut grass, it always makes my nose itch. One time I sneezed so hard because of it that I hit my head on the kitchen cabinet and the hinge completely popped off. We had to use this gray duct tape to keep the cabinet door shut for a whole month, and the tape left this awful sticky residue that never came off. Dust just sticks to it now and it looks all gray and fuzzy, like a caterpillar. I used to catch caterpillars in the backyard in a little plastic cup, but they always escaped.

You mentioned that since starting college two years ago, you've felt the same low mood the whole time. But I want to make sure I understand correctly — has there been even a few weeks or a month where you felt noticeably better, more like your normal self, before it went back to feeling this way?

No, I... I really don't think so. I haven't had any good weeks. It's just been the same heavy feeling every day. Like when you wake up and it's raining outside and the sky is that flat, gray color that makes everything look tired. 

My bedroom window looks out at the street, and when it rains, the water pools up in this big pothole right by the curb. Every time a car drives by, it splashes this huge wave of muddy water onto the sidewalk. Last week, this guy walking his dog got completely soaked. It was a golden retriever, I think, and the dog just shook itself off and got water all over the guy's pants. Dogs always shake from their head all the way down to their tail in this weird ripple motion. My neighbor has a dog that barks at the mailman every single day at exactly 11:30. The mailman wears these thick blue shorts even when it's freezing outside. I don't know how his legs don't get cold. I have to wear two pairs of socks just to walk around the house because the hardwood floors are always freezing. We have this one floorboard in the hallway that squeaks so loud if you step on it, it sounds exactly like a mouse getting stepped on. I always try to step over it, but I forget sometimes.
During these two years, have there been any times when you felt unusually energetic, like you needed less sleep than normal, or when your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Um, no, I don't... I haven't felt energetic at all. I'm always just tired. I definitely don't have racing thoughts or anything. My brain just feels really slow, like it's trudging through thick mud. 

Speaking of mud, when I was little I used to make these big mud pies in the backyard with my brother. We would decorate them with dandelion heads and little pebbles we found in the driveway. The driveway was made of that really loose gravel that always gets stuck in the tread of your shoes. I had these bright pink light-up sneakers that flashed every time I took a step. But one of the lights stopped working after I stepped in a huge puddle, so only my right foot lit up. It was so annoying to walk around like that, just flashing on one side. Like a broken street lamp. There's a street lamp outside my window that flickers all night long. It drives me crazy, it's just this constant buzzing sound like a giant mosquito trapped in a jar. I tried to catch a mosquito once, but I slapped my arm too hard and left this huge red handprint on my skin for like an hour.
Have there been any times during these two years when you felt really good, like unusually happy or optimistic, even if just for a few days?

No, I haven't had any days like that. I don't feel happy or optimistic at all, really. Just the same tired feeling. Like a balloon that's been sitting in the corner of a room for a week and it's all deflated and wrinkly. 

We had balloons like that after my cousin's birthday party last month. They were supposed to be helium, but I think the tank was almost empty because they barely floated. They were these metallic silver ones shaped like stars, but the points of the stars were all curled up. My aunt tried to tie them to the back of the chairs, but the ribbon was too short and she ended up just taping them to the wall. She used that really cheap, shiny scotch tape that always tears diagonally when you try to pull it off the dispenser. I hate when tape does that, you have to spend five minutes scratching at the roll with your fingernail just to find the edge again. My fingernails are always too short for that anyway because I bite them. I've tried putting that bitter-tasting polish on them, but it just makes all my food taste like chemicals. Especially sandwiches. I made a turkey sandwich yesterday and the bread got stuck to the roof of my mouth. It was that really soft white bread that squishes down to almost nothing when you press on it.

When you say it's been the same heavy feeling every day for two years, do you mean literally every single day without even one day where you woke up and felt a little bit lighter or better, even if just for a few hours?

No, I really mean it. It's just... every single day. I haven't woken up feeling lighter or better at all. It's just that same heaviness. Like trying to walk underwater in a swimming pool when you have all your clothes on. 

My friends pushed me into a pool once at a graduation party when I was fully dressed. I had on this denim jacket that got so heavy it felt like it was pulling me down to the bottom. The chlorine smelled so strong, it burned my nose for the rest of the night. You know how when you get water up your nose, it feels like a sharp needle right between your eyes? I hate that feeling. It's almost as bad as when you drink something freezing cold too fast and get brain freeze. I always get brain freeze when I drink milkshakes. Especially the strawberry ones from that diner down the street. They use real strawberries, but sometimes the chunks are too big and they get stuck in the straw. It's one of those paper straws that always gets soggy and collapses in the middle so you can't even suck anything through it anymore. I don't know why everyone switched to paper straws, they just dissolve in your drink and taste like cardboard. Cardboard boxes always smell weird to me, kind of dusty and old, like the attic in my grandma's house. She had these huge boxes up there filled with porcelain dolls that had those creepy glass eyes that follow you around the room.
During these two years, have there been any times when you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested, or when you were able to get a lot of things done that you normally couldn't?

Um, no... I don't think so. I haven't had any times where I needed less sleep or got a lot done. I always need sleep, but it never really helps. I just lay there and stare at the ceiling. 

My ceiling has these little bumps all over it, like cottage cheese. I used to try and find shapes in them when I couldn't sleep. Once I found one that looked exactly like a little dog with a curly tail, kind of like a pug. My neighbor used to have a pug named Barnaby, and he would snort constantly because his nose was so squished in. He sounded like a little pig rooting around in the dirt. Pigs are actually really smart, you know. I watched this documentary once about how they can learn tricks faster than dogs. But the documentary kept buffering because the internet at my house is terrible. The router is all the way in the basement, so by the time the signal reaches my room, it's basically gone. The basement always smells like mildew and old laundry detergent. We have this giant box of powdered detergent down there that's been sitting open for years, and the powder has turned into one solid rock because of the humidity. You'd probably need a hammer and chisel just to break off a piece to wash your clothes. I don't even know where our hammer is, probably lost in the garage somewhere under all those empty paint cans.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a two-year history of persistent depressed mood, anhedonia (loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities like knitting, journaling, and walking), fatigue, psychomotor retardation, and poor self-care (unchanged clothes for days). Notably absent are manic or hypomanic episodes, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, or periods of elevated mood. The patient explicitly denies any weeks or days of improvement over the entire two-year period. While the patient demonstrates tangential speech with excessive detail and difficulty maintaining focus (which could suggest ADHD or other conditions), the primary clinical presentation is consistent with Major Depressive Disorder. The onset coincided with stressor (starting college), but the persistent nature and lack of episodic variation support a depressive disorder rather than adjustment disorder.
